This public hearing this evening is to consider an application from Great Western Brewing Company to reason 519, second avenue north for mile one general light industrial to IH heavy industrial subject to a zoning agreement.
Now the subject property is the site of Great Western's existing operations located in the city park neighborhood and within Saskatoon City Center.
The site is currently zone dial one general light industrial and is designated as light industrial on the official community plan land use map.

Great Western site has operated as a brewery since 1927 when it was constructed for the hub city brewing company and it's recognized on the Saskatoon register of historic places for its heritage significance, including the near century of brewing on the property.

And it status is the last remaining major capacity brewing Saskatchewan. Great Western has indicated that several components of their facility are nearing or passed their end of life and they've identified a need for a modern brewing facility in order to continue operations.

They've considered a number of different options for their future, including moving to a new location, but have determined that their preferences to remain on their original site and constructing new facility here.
Now under the current zoning, the existing brewery is considered to be a non-conforming use as the aisle one zone does not permit breweries of the scale.
So in order to permit the construction of the new facility, a rezoning of the property is required.
So here's a view of the proposed site plan showing the proposed development.

A particular note is a new addition proposed on the southeast corner of the block that will house the new brewery and its components and be integrated with the existing 1927 structure that fronts along second avenue.

Here we're a changing configuration from nose and angle parking to parallel parking is necessary but I would note that with with the option chosen we have worked to ensure that the parking loss on 26 street is minimized and I'd also like to give my thanks and appreciation to both great Western and transportation for working collaboratively on a solution.

Now a policy analysis was also conducted as part of the internal review of this application to ensure that the proposal aligns with relevant sections of the official community plan and relevant secondary plans such as the city center plan in the city park local area plan and that's expanded on in appendix five of the report.

There are two facilitate the development of this proposal use of a zoning agreement is proposed as only agreement is a regulatory tool used to control the development of a specific piece of property through a legal agreement that is tied to land and ensures that only specific development proposal and specific land uses are what can be constructed and occur on the property.
The IH heavy industrial district will be used as the base zone for the agreement as it's the only zone within our bylaw that permits breweries of this particular scale.

Specific language of the zoning agreement will be restrictive so is to permit the brewery use and a limited range of commercial uses within the commercial space while prohibiting all other industrial uses that may ordinarily locate in the heavy industrial zone as well land use activities that generate excessive new senses or noxious effects will also be prohibited within the agreement in order to minimize the potential for land use conflicts.
The zoning agreement will also contain provisions that address parking landscaping and signage on site.
In conclusion city administration recognizes great westerns longstanding presence at this location and their significance within the city park and larger downtown area.
This proposed zoning agreement will facilitate the development of a new brewery that allows great western to remain on their site that has a brewing history of nearly 100 years.
The proposal is in conformance with the official community plan and relevant secondary plans as well as other requirements of the city.
